title: Nordhaus–Gaddum upper bound on chromatic numbers
statement: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$ with $n = \abs{V}$ vertices, and let $G^{c}$ denote its complement, the graph on $V$ in which two distinct vertices are adjacent precisely when they are non-adjacent in $G$. Writing $\chi$ for the chromatic number, the sum of the chromatic numbers of a graph and its complement satisfies \[ \chi(G) + \chi(G^{c}) \le n + 1. \]
hypotheses_covered: vertex set V is finite with n vertices
G^c is the complement of G
